partners.mechanism_chain: USP8 mutation (HGNC:12163) —DISRUPTS→ USP8 (HGNC:12163); USP8 (HGNC:12163) —INCREASES→ AKT pathway (R-HSA-4253195); AKT pathway (R-HSA-4253195) —LEADS_TO→ Pituitary adenoma (MONDO:0009050); PIK3CA mutation (HGNC:9475) —DISRUPTS→ PIK3CA (HGNC:9475); PIK3CA (HGNC:9475) —INCREASES→ AKT pathway (R-HSA-4253195); AKT pathway (R-HSA-4253195) —LEADS_TO→ Ovarian cancer (MONDO:0008170). Mutations in USP8 can lead to gain-of-function by disrupting its deubiquitinase activity, thereby increasing signaling through the AKT pathway, which is implicated in Cushing disease. Similarly, gain-of-function mutations in PIK3CA directly activate the AKT pathway, contributing to ovarian cancer development. Thus, dysregulation of the shared AKT pathway serves as a convergence point for these two diseases.

raw.translational: Targeting the MAPK and PI3K-Akt pathways with specific inhibitors has proven effective in treating various cancers, including lung cancer. Investigating the role of these pathways and their regulators in pituitary adenoma pathogenesis could reveal novel therapeutic strategies for Cushing disease, potentially leading to shared treatment approaches.
